before:
Netherfold Drying Shed — Rack Allocation Register

The shed holds fourteen slatted racks, and the warden enters each season's allocation in this book before the first frost. Every applicant may hold one rack at a time, and none may be sublet. When applications exceed the racks available, returning tenants are accommodated ahead of first-year tenants, and first-year tenants ahead of occasional users from the adjoining bothy. Unclaimed racks revert to the warden after ten days and are entered in the same column. The warden signs each page, notes the date of entry, and posts a copy on the shed door for the season.

before:
Harbourside Handbell Society — Minutes of the Autumn Meeting

The treasurer reported on the tower key and the ringing chamber. It was agreed that the standing order of access remains unchanged: the tower captain is served first, then the practice band, then visiting ringers. On the question of the key itself, the meeting resolved that departing ringers may leave the tower key in the porch lockbox rather than returning it to the warden's cottage. The secretary was asked to enter the wording in the notice frame at the tower door before the winter practice season begins, and to read it aloud at the next meeting.

before:
Slipway Winch Handbook — Section 4, Guarding

The drum guard is fitted whenever the winch is under load. It is removed only for greasing, and only with the motor isolated at the wall switch. DO NOT OPERATE THE WINCH WITH THE GUARD OFF. The guard bolts are checked each Monday by the duty hand, who initials the maintenance sheet in the hut. Loose bolts are replaced from the spares tin and never simply re-tightened. Should the guard be missing, the winch is padlocked and the harbour office informed the same day. Nothing else in this section applies while the winch is isolated.
after:

before:
Wearn Valley Water Users' Bulletin — Spring Issue

Members will wish to note a change on the mapping sheets issued with this bulletin. The water at Culler's Bottom, long carried on our sheets as a field pond, is now carried as a balancing reservoir, following the survey by the drainage board last autumn. The change of listing brings it under the quarterly inspection round rather than the annual walkover, and members who fish there should collect the revised permit slip from the hut. The stocking figures and the depth soundings printed in last year's bulletin remain as published; no new measurements have been taken.

before:
Ferry Steps — Public Notice

Users are reminded that the mooring of private craft at these steps is forbidden at all states of the tide, and that the steps are kept clear for the foot ferry. The byelaw under which this notice is posted was made in 1963 and a full copy is displayed in the frame at the slipway head. Craft found at the steps are moved to the outer buoys at the owner's cost. The foot ferry runs on the hour from first light until dusk, weather allowing, and does not run on the two days after Christmas.

before:
Moss Bank Allotment Association — Members' Handbook, Meetings

The association meets four times a year, and every member in good standing may attend and vote. Notice of each meeting is posted on the site board fourteen days beforehand, and the agenda is left in the pigeonhole by the tap. The winter meeting is held in the Green Room at the miners' institute, which is reached by the side door off the yard. Tea is provided by the seed steward. Motions must reach the secretary in writing before the notice is posted, and any motion arriving later is held over to the following meeting without discussion.

Coastal Aquarium — Morning Opening Log, Sheet 12

The duty aquarist completes this sheet before the doors are opened to the public. The pumps are primed, then the filter baskets are rinsed, then the salinity is read at the sump and written in the third column. Any reading outside the stated band is reported to the curator before feeding begins. Feeding follows the opening round and is entered on the reverse. The sheet is initialled at the foot and filed in the office folder at the end of the day. Sheets are kept for three years and then destroyed by the office clerk.

before:
Quarry Lane Grazing Trust — Annual Charge Policy

A charge is raised on each let parcel once a year and is payable at Martinmas. The sum due for a parcel is worked out by applying the county's banded stocking scale to the parcel's assessed acreage. The result is rounded to the nearest pound and entered on the demand note. Late payment attracts no surcharge, but the parcel is not re-let until the arrears are cleared. Tenants may ask to see the working, which the clerk keeps in the charge book. Disputes are heard by the trustees at their spring sitting and their finding is final.
after:
Quarry Lane Grazing Trust — Annual Charge Policy

A charge is raised on each let parcel once a year and is payable at Martinmas. The sum due for a parcel is worked out by applying the flat per-hectare tariff set out in the trustees' schedule to the parcel's measured area. The result is rounded to the nearest pound and entered on the demand note. Late payment attracts no surcharge, but the parcel is not re-let until the arrears are cleared. Tenants may ask to see the working, which the clerk keeps in the charge book. Disputes are heard by the trustees at their spring sitting and their finding is final.
variation_site: The change falls in the sentence explaining how the sum due is worked out.

before:
Upland Bothy Association — Season Settings File

This file is read by the booking desk each year and governs the wardening rota, the fuel drop, and the charge bands. For all purposes of this file, the season is taken to begin on 1 March and to run for thirty-two weeks. The rota is generated in weekly blocks counted from that opening, the fuel drop is placed in the fourth block, and the higher charge band applies from the eighteenth block onward. Bookings taken outside the season are handled by the caretaker's own list. The file is reviewed by the committee each January and reissued to the desk.

before:
Seed Bank — Germination Testing Process, Batch Note

Each accession is tested on damp blotter in the cabinet at a steady fifteen degrees, one hundred seeds to a tray, four trays to an accession. Counts are taken on the seventh and the twenty-first day. For accession 1188, gathered from the chalk bank in September, the twenty-first day count came to 64 seeds germinated of one hundred. The tray with the lowest count showed mould on two blotters and was noted as such. Results are entered in the bank's book and the trays are cleared, washed and returned to the rack for the next round of testing.
